title: Multi-Stage Mamba-Based Architecture for Fast and Scalable Superconducting Qubit Readout
authors: Luca Otting, Xiaorang Guo, Emmanouil Giortamis, Benjamin Lienhard, Pramod Bhatotia, Martin Schulz
abstract: Reliable qubit readout is a critical bottleneck toward fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC). In superconducting quantum processors, readout operations are both error-prone and high-latency. These challenges become more severe in frequency-multiplexed architectures, where signal crosstalk among neighboring qubits significantly degrades readout fidelity. Existing machine learning (ML)-based approaches rely on feed-forward neural networks (FNNs) that suffer from large parameter sizes and lack an end-to-end network that jointly addresses relaxation errors and discriminates qubit states.   In this work, we present a multi-stage qubit state discriminator based on the Mamba model, which enables efficient sequence modeling with linear complexity. The first stage performs initial state discrimination, followed by a refinement stage that identifies and mitigates relaxation-induced errors. Our lightweight model achieves a geometric mean readout fidelity of 0.906, outperforming the best-reported state-of-the-art method while reducing parameter size by 49.6%; our optimal model further reaches 0.911. Both models remain robust across varying input trace lengths, maintaining a high fidelity of 0.893 at readout durations as short as 500 $ns$, achieving up to a 26% reduction in logical error rate over prior work in quantum error correction (QEC).
summary: This paper introduces a novel, multi-stage qubit state discriminator built on the Mamba architecture to overcome readout bottlenecks in superconducting quantum processors. By achieving linear complexity and integrating error correction into the model, it significantly boosts readout fidelity and reduces logical errors compared to existing methods. This advancement is vital for realizing scalable fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_problem: Reliable qubit readout is a critical bottleneck for fault-tolerant quantum computing due to high error rates, latency, and signal crosstalk in multiplexed superconducting architectures.
main_result: The proposed Mamba-based discriminator achieves a geometric mean readout fidelity of 0.906 (optimal: 0.911) while significantly reducing model size and achieving up to a 26% reduction in logical error rate for QEC.
method: A multi-stage state discriminator is implemented using the Mamba architecture, which processes I/Q digitized traces with linear complexity, followed by an integrated error detection stage.
model_or_system: The system involves superconducting qubits read out via resonators, generating analog I/Q signals. The model uses a Multi-Stage Mamba architecture to process these time-series traces for single-qubit state discrimination.
key_observables: Readout fidelity (geometric mean), logical error rate reduction in QEC, and parameter size relative to prior FNN methods.
important_parameters: Short readout durations ($	ext{500 ns}$), crosstalk levels in frequency-multiplexed systems, and the required accuracy for fault tolerance.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that an efficient sequence model (Mamba) can jointly address state discrimination and relaxation errors better than traditional FNNs.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the readout pipeline from microwave pulse to classical processing, detailing the multi-stage discriminator architecture flow between the main classification model and the error detector.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the bottleneck of qubit readout in FTQC. It then introduces the Mamba-based multi-stage discriminator, detailing its two stages (initial discrimination and error refinement). Finally, it presents quantitative results comparing fidelity and logical error rate reduction against state-of-the-art methods.
why_interesting: The work directly addresses hardware limitations in quantum computing by proposing a computationally efficient ML model to improve the fundamental measurement process (readout), which is crucial for scaling up any quantum simulation or algorithm.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Readout pipeline of superconducting qubits. (a) On the QPUs side, the readout begins with a microwave pulse generated by the signal generator, then produces readout pulses that carry the qubit-state information. (b) On the classical side, the output signals are digitized into I/Q traces, which are then processed to determine the qubit states.
Fig. 3. Comparison between the main model’s predicted trace clusters (left) and the pseudo-ground-truth labels obtained from the KNN-based error detector (right).

Fig. 2. The basic structure of Mamba Model and its internal SSM layer. The input is normalized and processed by a convolutional layer, followed by an SSM layer that performs sequence modeling through recurrent hidden-state (h) updates using learnable matrices A, B, and C. A residual connection merges the input and output of SSM to form the final result.

Fig. 4. Architecture of the proposed multi-stage discriminator. The multi- stage workflow is shown on the left, while the right part illustrates the detailed Mamba architecture used in both the main classifier and the error detector.

Fig. 5. The heatmap illustrates the difference in error probability on a target qubit i conditioned on the prepared state of a spectator qubit j. Positive values (red) indicate a higher error rate on qubit i when qubit j is prepared in the |1⟩state compared to the |0⟩state.
